The Cyber Safe Girl project was initiated in 2016, inspired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao. In an increasingly digital world, this initiative extends that mission—Beti Bachao Cyber Crime Se. Women and young girls are often targeted in online frauds, scams, and exploitation, making cyber awareness a crucial part of their safety. Cyber Safe Girl 7.0 is a continuation of this mission, evolving with new threats such as fake
influencers, digital arrests, and AI-driven scams. By shedding light on these dangers, this book empowers readers with the knowledge and tools to protect themselves in the digital landscape.

Over the years, Cyber Safe Girl has become a trusted guide for students, professionals, and parents alike. Each new edition addresses the latest cyber crimes, backed by legal provisions and real-world cases, ensuring that readers stay informed and vigilant. As technology advances, so do cyber threats—but with awareness and the right precautions, we can outsmart cyber criminals. This book is not just a resource; it is a movement toward a safer digital future for every girl and woman.

The seventh edition of Cyber Safe Girl incorporates the latest cyber crime tactics and their corresponding legal implications under the IPC, BNSS, BSA, IT Act, and other relevant laws. It serves as a handbook for law enforcement, educators, and digital users, equipping them with the necessary insights to recognize, prevent, and respond to online dangers. Cyber security is not just about technology—it is about people, awareness, and collective responsibility. With this book, we take another step toward making cyberspace safer for all. Jai Hind!

FOLLOW THE 20-20-20 RULE: Every 20 minutes of screen time, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds to reduce eye strain.
2. USE BLUE-LIGHT BLOCKING GLASSES: Wear blue-cut lenses while using devices to reduce digital eye strain, especially in the evening.
3. ENABLE NIGHT MODE OR EYE COMFORT MODE: Most devices offer warm light filters — activate them after sunset.
4. AVOID SCREENS IN THE DARK: Do not look at screens in complete darkness — it strains your eyes and disturbs melatonin production.
5. KEEP A STRAIGHT POSTURE: Sit upright with your back supported and screen at eye level to avoid neck and back issues.
6. BLINK FREQUENTLY: Consciously blink often to avoid dry eyes while staring at screens.
7. TAKE TECH-FREE BREAKS: Designate at least 30–60 minutes a day without any digital devices.
8. AVOID SCREENS 1 HOUR BEFORE SLEEP: Exposure to screens before bedtime can affect your sleep quality.
9. KEEP DEVICES OUT OF THE BEDROOM: Make your sleeping area a gadget-free zone to ensure deeper sleep.
10. USE “DO NOT DISTURB” OR FOCUS MODES: These help in staying mindful and avoiding constant interruptions.
11. LIMIT SOCIAL MEDIA TIME: Use apps that track your usage and gently remind you to take breaks.
12. HYDRATE WELL: Drink water regularly — screen time often makes people forget to stay hydrated.
13. ADJUST SCREEN BRIGHTNESS TO MATCH ROOM LIGHTING: Avoid using very bright or dim screens in contrast with your environment - it reduces eye strain and helps maintain focus.
14. PRACTICE EYE EXERCISES: Simple activities like eye rolling or palm cupping can relieve tension.
15. STRETCH & MOVE: Get up every hour and do basic stretches or walk around to improve blood circulation.
